workLog.action: Reproduced the dead flag on the real fixture corpus
workLog.detail: eval-agent-vs-baseline --provider github-models --model openai/gpt-4o-mini exited 2 with "No pricing rate for model_id='openai/gpt-4o-mini'" before any API call. _plan_runner._estimate_cost_usd raises UnsupportedModelError for any id absent from MODEL_PRICING_RATES_USD_PER_1K_TOKENS, which is Anthropic-only, and that raise happens inside build_plan ahead of provider dispatch. The CLI already wrote args.provider into os.environ at line 1134, twenty lines before the build_plan call, so the seam existed and the plan simply never consulted it.
workLog.outcome: Issue 4002 filed with the reproduction and root cause

workLog.action: Decided the biller is the provider, not the model
workLog.detail: GitHub Models meters requests against an account allowance and publishes no per-token price. Inventing a USD rate would surface a fabricated number in an operator-facing cost report as though it were real, so no third-party rate was added. Printing $0.00 was rejected for the reason the aggregator's own docstring already gave: zero renders a free run and hides the missing price. cost_basis(provider) answers "requests" only for quota-billed providers and "usd" for everything else, so any per-token vendor added later inherits the strict raise-on-unpriced rule unchanged.
workLog.outcome: Design fixed before code, with the no-fabrication rule explicit

workLog.action: TDD red, then three atomic commits
workLog.detail: Nine tests written first: six plan-side, three aggregator-side. Confirmed red at 9 failed, 153 passed. Blast radius was seven files, over the five-file atomic ceiling, so the work was split: plan-time basis, then report-time basis, then CLI wiring and writer rendering. The basis helper moved into _eval_common the moment it gained a second consumer, because that module documents itself as the owner of pricing knowledge and a peer should not import an underscore-prefixed name from _plan_runner.
workLog.outcome: Commits 8f29248a4, 73dadb58d, 64800b5d9

workLog.action: Caught a defect I introduced, before pushing
workLog.detail: The new in-process CLI test called cli_main, which mutates global process environment. That value leaked into the pytest session and broke 10 downstream tests in a different module. Proven by isolation: that file alone passed 106, and with the new test running first it failed 10 and passed 97. Fixed by pinning EVAL_PROVIDER with monkeypatch in both new CLI tests. The underlying sharp edge is unchanged and real for any future in-process CLI test.
workLog.outcome: Self-caught before push; no downstream breakage shipped

workLog.action: Ran an adversarial review on a different model family
workLog.detail: The review returned three findings and all three reproduced. One: the plan read args.provider while the report read EVAL_PROVIDER, so selecting a provider through the environment alone made one run report two different bases. Two: eval-model-sweep crashed with a TypeError on float(None) when parsing a quota-billed child report. It now resolves provider exactly as _providers.resolve_provider does, (name or EVAL_PROVIDER or "anthropic").strip().lower(). Eight tests written first, four red. After the fix, env-only selection and the GitHub-Models spelling both report basis=quota, while the Anthropic control still prints cost_estimate_usd=2.22.

workLog.action: Fixed finding 2 in the model sweep

The sweep now carries the child's null through unchanged and records the child's own cost_basis beside it, rather than re-deriving an answer the child already settled. Serialization renders the null instead of substituting 0.0. Reports predating cost_basis read as usd, so old artifacts parse as before. Four tests written first, all four red with the TypeError.

workLog.action: Found the gate's cross-model refusal was dead for the rule kind
workLog.detail: The live extraction recorded upstream_model 'not-applicable' for a run that made 18 model calls. _provenance_mismatch compares every provenance key, upstream_model included, so it refuses to gate two extractions from different models. cmd_extract's rule branch never passed the report to _extract_provenance, so both sides recorded the same literal string and compared equal. Built a discrimination proof rather than asserting the bug: agent A sonnet vs agent B gpt-4o-mini refused with 'extraction parameter mismatch: upstream_model differs', while the rule pair returned no refusal. The protection exists and was missing for exactly one kind. Adding provider support is what made this reachable: an incumbent scored before the Anthropic cap and a challenger scored through GitHub Models after it would have been compared as though one model produced both.
workLog.outcome: Defect reproduced with a control before any code changed

workLog.action: Made the rule kind record the model and seed that produced its scores
workLog.detail: Two halves, committed separately because either alone is inert. Consumer: _rule_upstream_metadata returns the model and seed in the shape _extract_provenance already reads off an agent report, so the rule kind resolves upstream identity through the same code rather than a second copy. A second copy is exactly how the cost_basis defect happened earlier on this branch. Runs that disagree fail closed, for the same reason the envelope already requires matching rule names: reducing across runs assumes one population. Absent metadata records 'unknown-model', honest about ignorance, where 'not-applicable' asserted a falsehood. Producer: the report writes model_id and seed beside rules, not inside it, because a key inside would be scored as a rule name. 11 consumer tests written first with 10 red, 6 producer tests with 4 red.
workLog.outcome: Commits 700a66c46 and 1fd9174a0

workLog.action: Classified Copilot CLI as quota billed after the review found it fabricating
workLog.detail: Centralizing the dry-run decision in cost_basis was the right move, but the set that function reads was never audited against the provider registry. copilot and copilot-cli are registered transports that shell out to an authenticated GitHub Copilot CLI covered by a subscription, spend no per-token dollars, and were absent from the quota set, so they fell through the silent usd default. I checked the registry before accepting the finding, because adding a pricing opinion for a transport the tool cannot dispatch to would have been its own fabrication. Both names are registered, and the provider module documents copilot-cli as the preferred path, so the fabricated figure was live on the most recommended route. Reproduced on the real CLI: copilot-cli printed the sonnet input rate where github-models printed the requests line. Fixed the two names, then fixed the class: 17 tests pin every registry name to a declared basis and assert the registry and the classification cover the same set, so a new provider can no longer inherit a billing model by omission. outcomes.summary: --provider works. A non-Anthropic provider now plans, runs, and reports, proven by live evals through GitHub Models while the Anthropic account is budget-capped. The cost basis follows the transport that actually gets billed, so no fabricated USD figure can reach an operator-facing report or a dry-run plan, and no third-party price was invented to achieve it. All three optimizer kinds, agent, rule, and hook, now run on live data, and the rule kind records which model produced its scores so the gate's cross-model refusal works for it as it already did for agents.

learnings.primary: When two pieces of code answer the same question, the one that decides the consequence is the authority. cost_basis and resolve_provider both answered "which provider is this", and cost_basis answered differently. Because resolve_provider picks the transport that actually gets charged, any disagreement makes cost_basis wrong by construction, not merely inconsistent. The fix was not to add cases to a lookup but to delete the second answer and defer to the first.
secondary: dict.get's default does not fire when the key exists and holds None. Making a field nullable silently breaks every consumer that relied on that default, and those consumers do not appear in a grep of the diff.

An adversarial review on a different model family found three real regressions that my own None-safety audit missed, including a consumer in a module I never opened. All three reproduced; none was taken on the reviewer's word.
Proving a plan-time gate opens is not proving the capability works. The live run was the evidence that mattered, and it was cheap to get once the gate was open.

A required field filled with a placeholder passes validation and defeats the check it feeds. upstream_model is validated non-empty and compared by _provenance_mismatch to refuse cross-model gating. The rule kind auto-filled the literal 'not-applicable', which satisfied non-empty while carrying no information, so every rule comparison passed. A placeholder that is grammatically valid and semantically false is worse than a missing field, because the missing field would have raised.

Proving a capability on one input kind does not prove it on the others the same tool declares. The optimizer declares agent, rule, and hook. Running rule for the first time surfaced a dead gate protection immediately. A kind nobody has run is a kind nobody has tested.

A discrimination proof is stronger than a failure demonstration and costs one extra control. Showing the rule pair compared would have proved only that something was permissive; showing the agent pair refused through the same function established that the protection exists and was absent for exactly one kind, which told me which side to fix.

Correcting a fabricated session log does not correct the episode extracted from it. The commit hook only ever passes --preserve, which unions rather than replaces, so wrong content extracted once is permanent through the automatic path. --force exists and nothing invokes it. A correction mechanism that cannot reach a derived artifact leaves the derived artifact as the surviving copy of the error.

Centralizing a decision does not audit the data the decision reads. cost_basis became the single answer to which provider bills how, and the fix was correct, but the frozenset it consults still omitted two registered transports, so the defect stayed live on the provider the docs recommend most. The durable fix was not the two names, it was the test that pins every registry entry to a declared basis so omission stops being a silent classification.
